name: Jersey
summary: A red saltire on white with Jersey's badge in the upper part: three golden leopards (lions) on red, under the Plantagenet crown. The saltire had been used since the 18th century.
origin: Jersey used a red saltire on white from at least the late 18th century. In 1979 the States of Jersey decided to add the arms and a crown; the new flag was approved by Queen Elizabeth II and raised on 12 April 1981.

symbols.name: Saltire
symbols.meaning: Possibly from St Patrick's saltire, or chosen to distinguish Jersey's ships; its origin is uncertain.

symbols.name: Three leopards
symbols.description: Gold lions passant guardant on a red shield.
symbols.meaning: The Dukes of Normandy and the English Crown; Jersey was part of the Duchy of Normandy.

symbols.name: Plantagenet crown
symbols.description: A golden crown above the shield.
symbols.meaning: The island's allegiance to the Crown.

facts: Jersey is a Crown Dependency, not part of the UK.
Before 1981 its flag was confused with Ireland's St Patrick's saltire.
The three lions also appear on England's royal arms.
clues: A red saltire on white with a red shield of three gold lions under a crown.
Its lions come from a medieval duchy in France.
